Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seek quashing of FIR No.0499/2022 dated 30.07.2022 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S. Rajouri Garden, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 21.11.2022 arrived at between the parties before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi.
W.P.(CRL) 3736/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 21.11.2022 [Annexure-P-2(Colly)] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
3. Petitioner nos.1 to 5 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.

sentences.text: Learned ASC accepts notice.
She confirms that since the FIR involves matrimonial disputes, she has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 27.07.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement dated 21.11.2022 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.60,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 vide DD no.507181 issued on 12.12.2023 [ICICI Bank] in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present,
past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr. (2013) 4 SCC 58, W.P.(CRL) 3736/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
